>The US has warned China it must fulfil the terms of the trade war truce Donald Trump struck with Xi Jinping in Busan last year amid frustrations that Beijing is not living up to its commitments on exports of rare earths and other products.
>US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent and US trade representative Jamieson Greer delivered the message in a call on Friday morning with He Lifeng, the Chinese vice-premier in charge of trade negotiations with Washington.
>The warning comes two weeks before Trump and Xi are expected to meet in Shenzhen where China is hosting the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit. The FT reported last week that Xi may host a trilateral meeting with Trump and Russia’s President Vladimir Putin.
>The trade issue is not expected to be a large part of the Trump-Xi meeting in Shenzhen, but will almost certainly be discussed in more detail when the US and Chinese presidents meet at the G20 in Miami in December.
>In September, US officials told the FT that China was only fulfilling two-thirds of its Busan pledge on rare earths. One person familiar with the situation said Beijing had not increased the supply of rare earths since Bessent raised concerns directly with He in New York in September ahead of Xi’s Washington meeting with Trump.
>The US is also concerned about Chinese restrictions on the export of yttrium, a critical rare earth for everything from jet engines to missiles, to Japan, which produces components for products manufactured in America.
>Local companies have warned the Japanese government that their stockpiles are running dangerously low.
